records.label: Example
records.quote: M circle with radius length of 5 cm, XY = 12 cm
records.stem: In the figure opposite: M circle with radius length of 5 cm, XY = 12 cm, $\overline{MY} \cap$ circle M = {Z} and ZY = 8 cm. Prove that: $\overleftrightarrow{XY}$ is a tangent to circle M at X.
solution: $\because \overline{MY}\cap$ circle $M=\{Z\}$ ; $\therefore MY = MZ + ZY$
$\because MZ = MX = 5$ cm (radii) ; $\therefore MY = 5+8 = 13$ cm
$\therefore m(\angle MXY) = 90^\circ$ (The converse of the pythagorean theorem)
$\because \overleftrightarrow{XY} \perp \overline{MX}$
$\therefore \overleftrightarrow{XY}$ is a tangent to the circle at X. (Q.E.D)
records.answer: XY is a tangent to circle M at X

records.quote: Corollaries

records.quote: The line of centers of two touching circles passes through
records.claim: The line of centers of two touching circles passes through a point of tangency and is perpendicular to the common tangent.

records.label: Example
records.quote: Two circles M and N with radii length of 9 cm and 4 cm
records.stem: Two circles M and N with radii length of 9 cm and 4 cm respectively. Show the position of each of them with respect to the other in the following cases: A: MN = 13 cm; B: MN = 5 cm; C: MN = 3 cm; D: MN = zero; E: MN = 10 cm; F: MN = 15 cm.
solution: $\because r_1 = 9$ cm, $r_2 = 4$ cm $\therefore r_1 + r_2 = 13$ cm and $r_1 - r_2 = 5$ cm

parts.label: A
parts.stem: MN = 13 cm
solution: $\because MN = 13$ cm $\therefore MN = r_1 + r_2$ $\therefore$ the two circles are touching externally.

parts.label: B
parts.stem: MN = 5 cm
solution: $\because MN = 5$ cm $\therefore MN = r_1 - r_2$ $\therefore$ the two circles are touching internally.

parts.label: C
parts.stem: MN = 3 cm
solution: $\because MN = 3$ cm $\therefore MN < r_1 - r_2, MN \neq 0$ $\therefore$ circle N is inside circle M.
parts.answer: circle N is inside circle M

parts.label: D
parts.stem: MN = zero
solution: $\because MN = 0$ $\therefore$ the two circles are concentric.

parts.label: E
parts.stem: MN = 10 cm
solution: $\because MN = 10$ cm $\therefore r_1 - r_2 < MN < r_1 + r_2$ $\therefore$ the two circles are intersecting.

parts.label: F
parts.stem: MN = 15 cm
solution: $\because MN = 15$ cm $\therefore MN > r_1 + r_2$ $\therefore$ the two circles are distant.

records.label: Example
records.quote: M and N are two circles with radii length of 10 cm and 6 cm
records.stem: M and N are two circles with radii length of 10 cm and 6 cm respectively and are both touching internally at A, line AB is a common tangent for both at A. If the area of the triangle BMN = 24 cm^2 Find the length of segment AB.
solution: Since the two circles are touching internally at A, therefore A ∈ line MN, line MN ⊥ line AB
then the length of AB is the height of the triangle BMN whose base is MN
where: MN = 10 - 6 = 4 cm (why ?)
Area ΔBMN = 1/2 × MN × AB, therefore 24 = 1/2 × 4 × AB, therefore AB = 12 cm
records.notes: Printed '(why ?)' inside solution after MN = 10 - 6 = 4 cm.

records.label: Example
records.quote: the line of centers is perpendicular to the common chord
records.stem: Given: circle M ∩ circle N = {A, B}, CD is a diameter in circle M and CX is a tangent to circle M. R.T.P: Prove that m(∠DMN) = m(∠CEB).
solution: Proof: ∵ the line of centers is perpendicular to the common chord.
∴ MN ⊥ AB i.e. m(∠AFM) = 90°
∵ CD is a diameter in circle M and CX is a tangent at C
∴ CX ⊥ CD i.e. m(∠ECD) = 90°
∴ m(∠DMN) = m(∠CEF) (Q.E.D)
records.notes: Solution continues from previous page; given/R.T.P. printed here under 'Solution'. Printed 'why ?' is a prompt inside the solution.

objectives.label: Position of a point
objectives.description: Decide whether a point is outside, on, or inside a circle by comparing its distance from the centre with the radius.

objectives.label: Position of a line
objectives.description: Decide whether a line is outside, secant to, or tangent to a circle by comparing the distance from the centre to the line with the radius.

objectives.label: Tangent and radius
objectives.description: Use the relation between a tangent and the radius at the point of tangency to find measures and to prove a line is tangent.

objectives.label: Position of two circles
objectives.description: Decide the position of two circles (distant, touching externally, intersecting, touching internally, one inside the other, concentric) from the distance between centres and the radii.

objectives.label: Line of centers properties
objectives.description: Use the line of centers of touching or intersecting circles (common tangent, common chord) to find lengths and angles and to prove relations.
